Other hydrogen carriers besides ammonia and methanol include liquid organic hydrogen carriers and metal hydrides, but storage and transport of hydrogen via these methods are still at an R&D scale (DOE n.d.-h). 4.1.3 Liquified Natural Gas Production Technologies LNG is primarily produced from natural gas extracted from underground reservoirs. Drilling and hydraulic fracturing (fracking) are typically used to access the natural gas trapped in deep, hard rock formations like shale. The raw natural gas primarily consists of methane, but can also contain considerable amounts of ethane, propane, butane, and other heavier hydrocarbons. LNG can have compositional variability of the methane content, which affects fuel quality (Figure 35, data in Table A-1). The variability in composition of methane in LNG is primarily due to the natural gas source and processing technology employed (purification and liquefaction). Currently, no aviation fuel specification exists for LNG, and the creation of one would require narrow ranges in specification due to high compositional variabilities of LNG. This would require careful monitoring at airport fueling infrastructure to assess whether it has met aviation fuel specifications before use in aircraft, necessitating the need for additional fuel quality monitoring protocols. Another potential source of LNG is renewable natural gas (RNG). RNG, also referred to as biomethane, is upgraded biogas produced by the aerobic digestion of wastes—primarily from landfills, livestock operations, and wastewater treatment. The intermediary biogas comprises 45% to 65% methane, and the remainder is CO with trace amounts of contaminants (hydrogen 2 sulfide, siloxanes, and volatile organic compounds)(EPA 2024). Biogas is upgraded and purified to remove moisture, CO , and contaminants. The resulting RNG has methane content of at least 2 90%, and RNG transported in natural gas pipelines has a methane content between 96% and 98% (EPA 2024). While uncommon, RNG can be produced from the gasification of biomass feedstocks. RNG is used as an on-road transportation fuel in compressed natural gas medium- and heavy-duty vehicles. 55 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. Liquefaction of raw natural gas requires pretreatment to remove various impurities that pose danger to the processing equipment and the operation efficiency of the process. Some of the typical impurities in raw natural gas are water, dissolved salt, dust, CO , hydrogen sulfide (H S), heavy hydrocarbons, and mercury. These 2 2 impurities will be in a condensed state at cryogenic temperature or can cause corrosion that will ruin the liquefaction system’s sensitive components. To overcome these issues, the industry utilizes a variety of standardized pretreatment processes. These are typically dehydration to eliminate water; acid gas removal for CO and H S; and mercury removal to prevent corrosion of 2 2 aluminum-containing equipment and heavy hydrocarbon stripping.
